web.title: Tech selloff weighs down Wall Street as bond yields climb - Reuters
web.description:
Aug 18 (Reuters) - Wall Street's main indexes closed lower on Tuesday with semiconductors leading technology declines as Middle East uncertainty ​pushed bond yields to multiyear peaks, feeding concerns about borrowing costs and inflation.

The Philadelphia SE Semiconductor Index [(.SOX), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/quote/.SOX) tumbled 5% as investors fled stocks that had rallied previously on booming AI-related demand.

The S&P 500 [(.SPX), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/quote/.SPX) lost 53.30 points, or 0.69%, to 7,691.76 and the ​Nasdaq Composite [(.IXIC), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/quote/.IXIC) shed 355.20 points, or 1.33%, to 26,289.71, marking the biggest daily percentage decline since July 29 for both.

## CHIP COMPANIES A DRAG
The S&P 500's biggest drags from individual stocks came from chip companies, including leading AI chipmaker Nvidia [(NVDA.O), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/NVDA.O), down 2.3%, and memory chipmaker Micron Technology [(MU.O), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/MU.O), which fell 7% after ​rising almost 18% in the previous five sessions.

Other hard-hit stocks included data storage firms Sandisk [(SNDK.O), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/SNDK.O) and Western Digital [(WDC.O), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/WDC.O), which fell 9% and 7.4% respectively.

Aug 18 (Reuters) - Wall Street's main indexes closed lower on Tuesday with semiconductors leading technology declines as Middle East uncertainty ​pushed bond yields to multiyear peaks, feeding concerns about borrowing costs and inflation.

Fading hopes for Middle East peace pushed oil prices ‌higher, which in turn triggered an increase in U.S. 30-year Treasury bond yields to their highest levels since 2007. The 10-year bond yields touched their highest levels since January 2025.

Advertisement · Scroll to continue

The Philadelphia SE Semiconductor Index [(.SOX), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/quote/.SOX) tumbled 5% as investors fled stocks that had rallied previously on booming AI-related demand. Rising borrowing costs lowered how much investors were willing to pay for ​potential growth in technology profits.

"It starts off almost like a domino effect. Talks break down. That leads to oil prices going up. That ​leads to higher inflation expectations and bond yields rise," said Burns McKinney, portfolio manager at NFJ Investment Group. He ⁠added that "every time bond yields rise, that tends to disproportionately hit the technology names."

The S&P 500 [(.SPX), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/quote/.SPX) lost 53.30 points, or 0.69%, to 7,691.76 and the ​Nasdaq Composite [(.IXIC), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/quote/.IXIC) shed 355.20 points, or 1.33%, to 26,289.71, marking the biggest daily percentage decline since July 29 for both.

Advertisement · Scroll to continue

The Dow Jones Industrial Average [(.DJI), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/quote/.DJI) fell 116.38 ​points, or 0.22%, to 53,343.40.

## CHIP COMPANIES A DRAG

Among the S&P 500's 11 major sectors, information technology [(.SPLRCT), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/quote/.SPLRCT) created by far the biggest index-point drag and was the benchmark's biggest percentage loser, falling 1.9%.

The S&P 500's biggest drags from individual stocks came from chip companies, including leading AI chipmaker Nvidia [(NVDA.O), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/NVDA.O), down 2.3%, and memory chipmaker Micron Technology [(MU.O), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/MU.O), which fell 7% after ​rising almost 18% in the previous five sessions.

**\[5/5\]** Traders work on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) in New York City, U.S., August 7, 2026. REUTERS/Jeenah Moon/File Photo [Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/traders-work-on-the-floor-of-the-new-york-stock-exchange-nyse-in-new-york-city/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjY6bmV3c21sX1JDMlBUTUFRTFlJUQ%3D%3D/?utm_medium=rcom-article-media&utm_campaign=rcom-rcp-lead)

Other hard-hit stocks included data storage firms Sandisk [(SNDK.O), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/SNDK.O) and Western Digital [(WDC.O), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/WDC.O), which fell 9% and 7.4% respectively. The ​Roundhill Memory ETF tumbled 8.8% after five straight gains.

"There's nothing that can crack a momentum rally quite like interest rates moving higher and you're getting evidence of that today," ‌said Tony ⁠Welch, chief investment officer at SignatureFD, who added that rising yields suggested that Federal Reserve policy is too easy for the growth and inflation outlook.

Advertisement · Scroll to continue

Leaving high-growth sectors, investors flocked to more defensive sectors such as healthcare [(.SPXHC), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/quote/.SPXHC), which added 1.6%, and consumer staples [(.SPLRCS), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/quote/.SPLRCS), which finished up 1.1%. Wall Street's fear gauge [(.VIX), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/quote/.VIX) finished up 0.65 points at 15.84 for its highest close since August 4.

With support from rising oil prices, the S&P 500 energy sector [(.SPNY), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/quote/.SPNY) was the benchmark's biggest sector ​gainer on the day, adding 1.8%. By ​late afternoon, U.S. crude oil ⁠futures had pared most of their gains but still settled up 0.5%, after Iran threatened to shift to a "fully offensive" [military posture](https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/iran-threatens-go-offensive-strait-hormuz-if-diplomacy-with-us-fails-2026-08-17/) and Washington ruled out extending a ceasefire deal.

Shares of home-improvement retailer Home Depot [(HD.N), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/HD.N) eased 0.1%, even after it ​beat [second-quarter sales estimates](https://www.reuters.com/business/retail-consumer/home-depot-beats-quarterly-sales-estimates-steady-repair-demand-2026-08-18/).

Investors awaited results due later this week from other retailers, including bellwether Walmart [(WMT.O), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/WMT.O). Minutes from the ​Fed's July meeting, due ⁠on Wednesday, could offer more clues about how the central bank is assessing the current environment.

Investors see Nvidia's upcoming quarterly report as the next big test for the AI-driven momentum.

Declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 1.94-to-1 ratio on the NYSE, where there were 169 new highs and 252 new lows. On the Nasdaq, 1,778 ⁠stocks rose and ​2,977 fell as declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 1.67-to-1 ratio.

The S&P 500 posted 10 ​new 52-week highs and four new lows while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 75 new highs and 121 new lows.

On U.S. exchanges, 14.86 billion shares changed hands, compared with the 16.88 billion moving ​average for the last 20 sessions.

Reporting by Sinéad Carew in New York, Shashwat Chauhan and Purvi Agarwal in Bengaluru; Editing by Shilpi Majumdar and Rod Nickel

US stocks fell on Tuesday as tech stocks sold off and elevated oil prices and government bond yields weighed on markets.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite ( [^IXIC](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/%5EIXIC/)) fell 1.3%, leading the major indexes lower. The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( [^DJI](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/%5EDJI/)) declined by 0.2%, while the S&P 500 ( [^GSPC](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/%5EGSPC/)) pulled back by 0.6%, extending losses after [a downbeat start to the trading week.](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/live/stock-market-today-monday-august-17-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-oil-treasurys-094421171.html)

7,691.76 -53.30 (-0.69%)

At close: August 18 at 4:38:24 PM EDT

^GSPC^DJI ^IXIC

Oil prices climbed to their highest level in over two weeks after President Trump said he intends to inflict more economic pain on Iran and [threatened to "bomb" Oman](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/well-bomb-the-s-out-of-them-trump-threatens-oman-as-it-reportedly-moves-toward-a-deal-with-iran-155621451.html) if it interferes with the US's plans for the Strait of Hormuz.

Brent crude ( [BZ=F](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/BZ=F/)) futures, the international benchmark, traded near $91 per barrel, and US benchmark West Texas Intermediate crude futures ( [CL=F](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/CL=F/)) rose to $84 per barrel as the US Strategic Petroleum Reserve plunged to its [lowest level since 1982](https://finance.yahoo.com/energy/article/the-strategic-petroleum-reserve-hasnt-been-this-low-since-reagan-was-filling-it-in-1982-critics-wonder-how-low-is-too-low-180740733.html).

Rising oil, [an AI borrowing spree](https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/articles/ai-driving-treasury-yields-just-093000747.html?.tsrc=372&ncid=crm_-2240951-20260817-0--A&bt_user_id_proof=MYmKMtbFxMgc3XAqiUPZn33g1jr6OV2xnexP285aBXsSw1VyJkYotJmm3SffjYrrKaRDUhgvmsyD2O3a1twjSTenUJjfJjRupbWoA4Ad%2Feb6NbGeLUvzvsdQHtCVhdNL&bt_ts_proof=1787005901660), and concerns over government borrowing have also lifted bond yields globally in recent days. The 10-year Treasury yield ( [^TNX](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/%5ETNX/)) eased somewhat but remained elevated at 4.70%, and the 30-year yield ( [^TYX](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/%5ETYX/)) held near a 19-year high.

Earnings, meanwhile, have supported equities so far this reporting season. While the second quarter reporting period has slowed, Home Depot's ( [HD](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/HD/)) stock was little changed after reporting an improvement in sales for the second quarter as customers leaned toward smaller projects over the summer, and Klarna ( [KLAR](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/KLAR/)) [stock plunged on a trimmed outlook.](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/klarna-stock-plunges-20-on-trimmed-guidance-as-german-retail-sales-slow-141517463.html)

# Stock Market News, August 18, 2026: Tech Stocks Slide With Global Bond Selloff Picking Up Steam

## Growing fiscal deficits, inflation fears and massive AI spend are pushing up borrowing costs

Created with Highcharts 9.0.1Stock-index performanceSource: FactSetAs of Aug. 18, 4 p.m. ET

Created with Highcharts 9.0.1Aug. 14Aug. 18-2.25-2.00-1.75-1.50-1.25-1.00-0.75-0.50-0.2500.25%DowS&P 500Nasdaq

Stocks sold off Tuesday with borrowing costs around the world near multiyear highs, as investors fret over heavy fiscal spending and inflation.

The 30-year U.S. Treasury yield rose as high as 5.337%, its highest intraday level since 2007; [Japanese long-dated yields](https://www.wsj.com/livecoverage/stock-market-today-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-08-18-2026/card/what-s-driving-the-worldwide-bond-selloff-sLKr2W77rjTT9NsXoBlK) ended the day at their highest level since at least 2006. One factor pushing up yields: The capital-hungry AI industry’s [huge appetite for debt](https://www.wsj.com/livecoverage/stock-market-today-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-08-18-2026/card/-money-quote-the-bond-deluge-driving-today-s-selloff-l3BYSkm4kAPHWvZ6ApyL), which puts it in competition with traditional nation-state borrowers.

Equities also struggled, with the Nasdaq down 1.3% on the day. Chip stocks were hit hard, with the PHLX Semiconductor index down more 5% and some of its components (Intel, Marvell, ARM Holdings, Coherent, and Teradyne) off more that that.

Renewed tensions in the Middle East are also weighing on markets. Iran [fired two ballistic missiles](https://www.wsj.com/world/middle-east/irans-attacks-on-ships-in-hormuz-pile-up-testing-u-s-military-restraint-6ff9f5dd) toward the strait on Tuesday, triggering air defenses in the United Arab Emirates, according to that country’s Ministry of Defense. Earlier Tuesday, an Iranian attack hit a bulk carrier in the strait east of Oman.

The attacks came after a 60-day truce between the U.S. and Iran expired yesterday with few signs of progress towards a permanent deal to replace it. President Trump wrote this morning that no talks are planned with Iran. Brent crude oil prices edged higher to $91.02 a barrel.

🔎 Dig deeper into markets with our [daily wrap-up](https://www.wsj.com/finance/investing/bonds-are-getting-hammered-and-wall-street-says-the-rout-wont-end-anytime-soon-895e0ad8) or listen to the WSJ [Minute Briefing](https://www.wsj.com/podcasts/minute-briefing/chip-makers-take-stock-indexes-into-the-red/d045f0ff-f52d-4749-9b4f-a5301b48012b) podcast.

# Broadcom and Intel Shares Extend Losses as Chip Selloff Deepens

### June 5th, 2026 -

About 1 Mins

![](https://www.cmelitegroup.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/shutterstock_2454837739.jpg)

![Dotted Circle](https://www.cmelitegroup.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/dotted-Circle.png)

![Dotted Circle Alt2x](https://www.cmelitegroup.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/dotted-Circle_alt2x.png)

The chip selloff is continuing. Broadcom shares dropped another 1.9% in premarket trading on Friday after falling 13% on Thursday, wiping out about $286 billion in market value in one day. This was the fourth-largest single-day loss for any U.S. company. The rest of the semiconductor sector is also down for a second day. Here’s what caused the selloff and whether the chip rally that pushed markets to record highs is losing steam.

Thursday’s drop started after Broadcom released its fiscal second-quarter earnings. While results were better than expected, the company’s revenue outlook fell short. Investors were also unsettled when the CEO said on the earnings call that Google, a major custom-chip client, might look for other suppliers. That news hurt the stock more than the financial results did.

Losses continued across the sector on Friday. Micron Technology fell 3.2%, Advanced Micro Devices dropped 3.2%, Intel lost 3.1%, and Marvell Technology was down 3.6% in premarket trading. The PHLX Semiconductor Index is up 92% in 2026, but it fell more than 2% on Thursday, making some wonder if the rally is slowing down.

The two-day drop does not mean the cycle is over. Top chip companies like Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing, and Micron are still expected to do better than the overall market, even if their gains slow down from earlier this year. As investors become more selective, the gap between leading companies and the rest of the sector will likely grow in the coming months.
